name: MAX98357AETE+T
title: MAX98357A/MAX98357B: mono Class D speaker amplifier with a PCM (I2S, left-justified, TDM) digital input
summary: A mono filterless Class D amplifier that takes digital PCM audio directly: BCLK, LRCLK and DIN in, a bridged speaker drive out, with no master clock and no register setup. The A version reads I2S data and the B version left-justified data; both also take 8-slot TDM, at sample rates of 8 kHz to 96 kHz. One pin (SD_MODE) shuts the part down or picks left, right or the average of both; a second (GAIN_SLOT) sets 3 to 15 dB of gain, or the TDM slot. It runs from 2.5 V to 5.5 V and gives 3.2 W into 4 Ω at 5 V and 10% THD+N, in a 9-bump WLP or a 3 mm x 3 mm 16-pin TQFN.

notes: A + in the part number marks a lead-free, RoHS-compliant package; T marks tape and reel; /V marks the automotive-qualified part.

The A and B versions differ only in the serial format they read: A takes I2S, B takes left-justified data. Both take TDM; in TDM the A samples data on the rising BCLK edge and the B on the falling edge.

pins.name: SD_MODE
pins.function: Shutdown when held low. In I2S or left-justified mode its voltage picks the output channel (left, right, or the average of both; see the SD_MODE control table). In TDM mode it works with GAIN_SLOT to choose the slot. Has an internal 100 kΩ pulldown.

pins.name: GAIN_SLOT
pins.function: In I2S or left-justified mode, sets the gain by how it is tied (see the gain table). In TDM mode, chooses the slot together with SD_MODE; gain is then 12 dB.

pins.name: LRCLK
pins.function: Frame clock: the left/right word clock in I2S and left-justified mode, the frame-sync pulse in TDM mode.

pins.name: GAIN_SLOT
pins.function: In I2S or left-justified mode, sets the gain by how it is tied. In TDM mode, chooses the slot together with SD_MODE; gain is then 12 dB.

pins.name: SD_MODE
pins.function: Shutdown when held low; otherwise its voltage picks the output channel (I2S/LJ) or, with GAIN_SLOT, the TDM slot. Internal 100 kΩ pulldown.

pins.name: LRCLK
pins.function: Frame clock: word clock in I2S/LJ mode, frame-sync pulse in TDM mode.

pins.name: EP
pins.function: Exposed pad, with no internal connection. Solder it to a solid ground plane to carry heat away.

operation.text: BCLK, LRCLK and DIN carry the audio. With a 50% duty LRCLK, the format follows the part: the MAX98357A reads I2S, with the data word starting one BCLK after the LRCLK edge, and the MAX98357B reads left-justified data, with the word starting on the LRCLK edge. When LRCLK is a short frame-sync pulse instead, both switch to TDM on their own; the pulse marks the start of slot 0. I2S and left-justified data may be 16, 24 or 32 bits; TDM data 16 or 32 bits, in up to eight slots. No master clock is used.

LRCLK may be 8, 16, 32, 44.1, 48, 88.2 or 96 kHz. 11.025, 12, 22.05 and 24 kHz are not supported. BCLK must be 32, 48 or 64 times LRCLK. LRCLK must not be stopped while BCLK runs: that can drive the output to a large DC level.
The interface tolerates 0.5 ns RMS jitter below 40 kHz and 12 ns of wideband RMS jitter on BCLK and LRCLK while keeping more than 98 dB dynamic range.

On the MAX98357A, LRCLK low marks the left word; on the MAX98357B, LRCLK high marks it. In I2S and left-justified mode both parts take data on the rising BCLK edge. In TDM mode the A takes data on the rising edge and the B on the falling edge.
The interface has a DC-blocking high-pass filter with its -3 dB point at 3.7 Hz.

If BCLK stops, the part drops into standby by itself: the output stage turns off and both outputs go high impedance so no current flows into the speaker. Standby draws 340 µA typical, more than the 0.6 µA of full shutdown; it serves where no GPIO is free to pull SD_MODE low.

A digital lowpass after the interface removes aliasing and other high-frequency content. Its type follows the sample rate: an IIR voice filter below 30 kHz, and FIR audio filters from 30 to 50 kHz and above 50 kHz (see the digital filter settings table).

SD_MODE low (below B0) shuts the part down: every block is off and the outputs are high impedance, drawing under 0.6 µA typical. Driven high (above B2) it plays the left word. Pulled up through RSMALL it settles between B1 and B2 against the internal 100 kΩ ±8% pulldown and plays the right word; pulled up through RLARGE it settles between B0 and B1 and plays (left + right)/2. RSMALL and RLARGE depend on the logic-high voltage of the driver (see the equations and the examples table). The resistor may hang from an open-drain GPIO (resistor from VDDIO to SD_MODE, GPIO pulling the node low) or sit in series with a push-pull GPIO.

In left-channel mode SD_MODE is driven straight to the logic high, which must not exceed the pin's absolute maximum of VDD + 0.3 V. Keeping VDD above VDDIO avoids this. Where that cannot be held (for example VDD < 3.0 V with VDDIO = 3.3 V), about 2 kΩ in series with SD_MODE limits the current into the pin. The right and (left/2 + right/2) modes already have a series resistor.
The only general start-up rule is that LRCLK starts within half an LRCLK period of BCLK starting. Click-and-pop performance is the same whether the clocks start before or after SD_MODE rises.

With BCLK at 256 kHz (LRCLK 8 kHz) the part powers up correctly only if: BCLK and LRCLK are not applied before the part is enabled; both start low and then go high; they start at least 10 µs after VDD exceeds 2.3 V and SD_MODE is high (the 10 µs counts from whichever comes last); LRCLK starts at least half a BCLK and no more than half an LRCLK after BCLK; LRCLK completes whole cycles only; and once running, both clocks keep running without a break. To stop them, set SD_MODE to 0 V first, and repeat the same sequence on the next start.

TDM is recognised from the short sync pulse on LRCLK, and the bit depth from the clock ratio. A frame holds 128 BCLK cycles with 16-bit slots or 256 with 32-bit slots. Gain is fixed at 12 dB, and SD_MODE with GAIN_SLOT chooses which of the eight slots the part plays (see the TDM channel selection table).

The bridged Class D output needs no LC filter: edge-rate and overshoot control together with spread-spectrum modulation keep emissions low while efficiency reaches 92%. The switching frequency moves at random by ±20 kHz around 300 kHz; above 10 MHz the spectrum looks like noise.
When the output current passes the 2.8 A typical limit, the outputs turn off for about 100 µs and then back on. This repeats for as long as the fault stays.
The amplifier has thermal-overload protection as well as short-circuit protection.

In I2S and left-justified mode GAIN_SLOT sets five gains: 15 dB to GND through 100 kΩ, 12 dB to GND, 9 dB open, 6 dB to VDD, 3 dB to VDD through 100 kΩ (resistors ±5%). The gain is referred to the DAC full-scale output of 2.1 dBV. In TDM mode gain is 12 dB.

At start-up the signal ramps from mute to full level. On entering shutdown both outputs drop to GND together, with no volume ramp-down; ramping the digital data down before shutdown gives the quietest result. Power-up and power-down order does not change the click-and-pop result.

With no output filter, the speaker's own inductance and the ear do the filtering, and the 300 kHz switching moves the cone very little. Use a speaker with more than 10 µH series inductance; typical 8 Ω speakers have 20 µH to 100 µH.

Bypass VDD to GND with 0.1 µF and 10 µF. Some designs need only the 10 µF, so the part can run with one external component (a 4.32 mm² solution with the WLP). Long supply traces call for extra bulk capacitance at the part.

Keep output, supply and ground traces wide and low in resistance; they also help the part shed heat. Trace resistance costs power at low load impedance: 2 W into 4 Ω becomes 1.904 W at the speaker through 100 mΩ of total trace and 1.951 W through 10 mΩ. Capacitance on the output traces raises quiescent current (see the equations). Ground fill around signal traces on the outer layers helps RF immunity.

The WLP pinout lets 6, 9 or 12 dB gain be set without a via or a trace out of the centre bump: for 12 dB the centre bump (GAIN_SLOT) is tied to the GND bump beside it. An example layout for left-channel playback at 12 dB occupies 1.78 mm x 2.49 mm.

circuits.title: Left-channel PCM operation with 6dB gain
circuits.description: One amplifier on the codec's I2S (MAX98357A) or left-justified (MAX98357B) bus. GAIN_SLOT tied to VDD sets 6 dB. SD_MODE is driven straight from a codec GPIO: high plays the left word, low shuts the amplifier down. The speaker sits across OUTP and OUTN with no filter; VDD has a 10 µF and a 0.1 µF capacitor to ground.

circuits.title: Left-channel PCM operation with 12dB gain
circuits.description: The same left-channel connection with GAIN_SLOT tied to ground, which sets 12 dB. GPIO high plays the left word; GPIO low shuts the amplifier down.

circuits.title: Right-channel PCM operation with 6dB gain
circuits.description: Right-channel playback at 6 dB (GAIN_SLOT to VDD). SD_MODE is fed from the GPIO through RSMALL, so with the GPIO high the pin settles between the B1 and B2 trip points against the internal 100 kΩ pulldown and the right word is played. GPIO low shuts the amplifier down.

parts.note: RSMALL; the value is for a 1.8 V GPIO

circuits.title: (Left/2 + Right/2) PCM operation with 6dB gain
circuits.description: Mono playback of the average of both words at 6 dB. SD_MODE is fed from the GPIO through RLARGE, which puts the pin between the B0 and B1 trip points when the GPIO is high. GPIO low shuts the amplifier down.

parts.note: RLARGE; the value is for a 1.8 V GPIO

circuits.title: Stereo PCM operation using two ICs
circuits.description: Two amplifiers share BCLK, LRCLK and DIN from the codec, and one GPIO enables both. U1 takes SD_MODE directly from the GPIO and plays the left word; U2 takes it through RSMALL and plays the right word. Both have GAIN_SLOT on VDD for 6 dB, their own 10 µF and 0.1 µF supply capacitors and their own speaker. GPIO low shuts both down.

parts.note: RSMALL; the value is for a 1.8 V GPIO

circuits.title: Channel TDM operation (gain fixed at 12dB)
circuits.description: Four amplifiers on one TDM bus, each picking its own slot while gain is fixed at 12 dB. All four take SD_MODE straight from the codec GPIO (high = on, low = shutdown); GAIN_SLOT then selects the slot: to ground for slot 0 (U1), to VDD for slot 1 (U2), unconnected for slot 2 (U3), and to VDD through 100 kΩ for slot 3 (U4). Each amplifier has a 0.1 µF and a 10 µF supply capacitor and its own speaker.
